content:
Rushing to officially launch macOS 27 Golden Gate later this year, Apple continues to push forward with test versions, releasing the fifth beta to developers today. Here's what you can expect.

Apple releases macOS 27 beta 5

Three weeks ago, Apple released macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 4, and a corresponding public beta was also released shortly after.

The company is now releasing macOS Golden Gate beta 5, continuing its efforts to fix bugs and performance issues in preparation for the official version later this year.

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a brand-new Siri app, along with a redesigned Siri AI. The system also features a new AI-powered version of the Shortcuts app, which can accept natural language commands to create shortcuts, and provides an instruction-based Safari extension builder.

Additionally, macOS 27 Golden Gate adds new Golden Gate-themed wallpapers and screensavers, while reverting the rounded corners of windows and apps back to a fixed radius. This change reverses a modification introduced in macOS 26, which adjusted the corner radius based on the content of each window or app's menu bar.

The build number for macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 5 is 26A5406e. We are currently examining this new beta closely and will report back to you with our findings later.

How to install macOS 27 Golden Gate beta

Below are the steps to install macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 5:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the "i" icon next to "Beta Updates"
  • Select "macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta" from the drop-down menu in the top right corner
  • Press "Done"

Have you discovered any new features in this macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
